披.meaning: Dragging her <part>anchor</part> across a sandbank, a fisher hooks a buried <part>pelt</part> and hauls it up, sand pouring off. Rolled inside it is a treasure map, laid bare to the sky for the first time in a hundred years. The tide has decided to <kanji>expose</kanji> it.
披.on: She pins the map down with the <sound>hee</sound>l of her boot so the wind can't take it.

堆.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> wants the best view in the park, so it carries <part>soil</part> in its beak, crumb by crumb, all summer long. By autumn its little mound is taller than the park bench. The bird perches proudly on top of earth <kanji>piled high</kanji>.
堆.on: It wears a tiny <sound>tie</sound> for the opening ceremony.
堆.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>ps,' it chirps, dropping a yu<sound>zu</sound> seed, a <sound>ta</sound>co crumb and a <sound>ca</sound>lm little snail onto the top.

僕.meaning: At a midnight station, a tired <part>porter</part> hangs fifty coats on one <part>coat hook</part> and stacks fifty suitcases beside it without a wobble. The station master gasps, 'Who did all this?' The porter taps his chest and smiles: '<kanji>Me</kanji>.'
僕.on: His only helper, a <sound>box</sound>er dog, wags at the praise.
僕.kun: '<sound>She</sound>'s next,' says the boss, so he fetches a <sound>mo</sound>p for the cleaner and then makes up her <sound>be</sound>d: a servant's night.

箇.meaning: An explorer leaves a fresh <part>bamboo</part> stalk to <part>harden</part> in the desert sun, then snaps it into neat little tags. On each one she writes a thing in her pack: rope, map, teapot. Now everything she carries has its own tag, one per <kanji>item</kanji>.
箇.on: The last tag goes on a paper kite shaped like a <sound>ca</sound>rp.

貢.meaning: In a sea cave, an old otter sits at his <part>workbench</part> and polishes the finest <part>shellfish</part> shell he can find until it gleams like a pearl. He swims it to the lighthouse keeper who once saved him and leaves it on her step: a <kanji>tribute</kanji>.
貢.on: She thanks him with an ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne, which he eats on his back in the waves.
貢.kun: '<sound>Me</sound>? For me?' she asks, then sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' in the sea spray.

塀.meaning: Two neighbours argue over a strip of <part>soil</part> between their gardens. One plants a <part>flag</part> in it; the other drags in old <part>rugby posts</part> and nails planks between them. By sunset a tall line of planks splits the plot in two: a <kanji>fence</kanji>.
塀.on: They stuff the gaps with <sound>hay</sound> so neither can peek at the other's roses.

韻.meaning: Every time the door <part>chime</part> dings, a bored bank <part>employee</part> must greet the customer in verse: 'Welcome, sir, the rain is cold; would you like to save your gold?' The queue claps. Her manager insists every greeting must <kanji>rhyme</kanji>.
韻.on: She writes each one down in purple <sound>in</sound>k for the staff noticeboard.

昭.meaning: From her balcony, an opera singer sends one long high <part>call</part> up at the grey sky. The clouds split, and the <part>sun</part> pops out as if to take a bow, flooding the street with light. Every window in town is <kanji>shining</kanji>.
昭.on: The neighbours cheer from their rooftops at the best <sound>show</sound> of the year.
